title: Why Is It Thailand’s Fault That Stupid Tourists from Stupid Prohibitionist Countries Try to Smuggle Out Cannabis?
description: Thailand, which actually means “Land of the Free”, is being pressured into sharply restricting cannabis sales because foreign tourists have been ca...
content_html_sanitized:
Thailand, which actually means “Land of the Free”, is being pressured into sharply restricting cannabis sales because foreign tourists have been caught trying to smuggle suitcase quantities of cannabis back to the UK.

The political problem is complicated by the fact that the Thai ruling coalition is divided between a Prohibitionist party and an anti Prohibitionist party. Forcing recreational cannabis back into the black market would be a disaster for Thailand. Cannabis is very popular with the Thai people, and the Thai economy benefits from cannabis tourism. It should focus on sensible regulations, and keeping the market for cannabis separate from hard drugs.

See “More than 50 British nationals have been arrested in the country for attempting to smuggle cannabis since July 2024, according to a joint operation between the UK government and Thai authorities.”

Plus, “The UK government reports, International crackdown on

cannabis smuggling. UK-Thai cooperation results in 90% reduction in cannabis arriving in the post.”

Meanwhile, back in the U.K., cannabis prohibition is a disaster. See Why Is the UK Still Failing Children Who Need Medical Cannabis? And Scotland Forever? Not With This Drugs Policy!

But really, why is the stupidity of British tourists and, especially British lawmakers, a problem for Thailand? Do a search for “cannabis” on BBC.com or any UK news website, and it will be immediately obvious that cannabis prohibition is a disastrous, counterproductive fraud.

Finally, consider this from the US National Library of Health: “The number of admissions to hospitals in England for reasons specifically to do with alcohol has more than doubled over the past 12 years, warns a new report. The statistics also show a big increase in the number of prescriptions for drugs to treat alcohol dependency.”

And the Thai cannabis community is fighting back. See Cannabis Advocates Warn of Fallout from Thailand’s New Medical Use Rule “Cannabis advocates in Thailand are voicing frustration over a new proposal from the Public Health Ministry that would require all cannabis users to present medical certificates, restricting its use solely to medical purposes.

Daycha Siripatra, a respected traditional medicine practitioner, criticised the move as a significant barrier to accessing cannabis for alternative treatments. He stressed the importance of public engagement in shaping the policy, warning that ignoring public sentiment could provoke the backlash—especially from those who have heavily invested in the cannabis industry following decriminalisation.”  

Stay tuned. The United Kingdom owes the Kingdom of Thailand an apology. Meanwhile, just for giggles, read about the First Opium War.
